integrity: The proof is algebraic and complete: the fixed-point equation is equivalent to a(b-a^2)=c(c-1)(c+1). For c>=2 every positive divisor produces a valid base, and fixed-leading-digit admissibility is exactly a congruence modulo a whose local solution counts are computed at every prime power. Finite checks are corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only exactly two-digit fixed points of the cubic digit-sum map while the base varies. It does not classify larger fixed points or nontrivial cycles. The divisor identity is elementary, but the result also proves that every divisor is digit-valid for c>=2 and gives an exact CRT residue-density law for fixed leading digit. An equivalent varying-base parametrization may exist in unindexed perfect-digital-invariant literature.
title: Divisor and residue structure of two-digit cubic happy fixed points
